P1.evidence: The first eleven minutes were lost to the prospect's audio failing. When it worked the rep went straight to a logistics negotiation about running short or rebooking — 'usually these meetings run at least 45 minutes... we just jump back on at 3pm... How does that sound?' — then opened on nutrition. No setter-note readback, no four-part frame, no frame agreement. The nearest thing to an opening question came 19 minutes in: 'Well, what's your goal?'

P2.evidence: Three of nine run. Nutrition asked directly ('how is your nutrition at the moment?'), energy asked with a scale ('not like a skill from one to 10'), and injuries asked and then usefully re-asked when the prospect misread the question ('What I mean with mobility is mainly like, do you feel like you have something in your back sometimes, in your shoulders, like aches?'). Age and start weight were volunteered unprompted and the rep only probed current weight ('So like 150 or something, then?'); height never established. Nothing on desk-bound work, health conditions or hereditary risk, training week, results, or sleep — and the prospect flagged sleep himself ('a little bit of stress, bed as well, actual sleeping') and the rep let it go.

P3.evidence: The strongest phase. Clean bridge to the why — 'there's always a why behind why we want to get better in physical shape... So what do you feel like is your big why' — and a clean identity payoff — 'What does that mean to you and how would you look at yourself when you are actually that person?' → 'Unstoppable.' Reflected the picture back and checked it: 'Is that the clear picture or am I missing something there?' Two gaps: he never asked what physical thing the prospect cannot do (rugby was volunteered), and he never asked who else this impacts, on a call where the prospect had already named a daughter he is fighting for and a dying mother.

P4.evidence: 'Why do you feel like you didn't stick with that program?' produced the root cause cleanly — 'Weak-minded, weak-willed... I've been a people-pleaser most of my life' — and 'what do you need for yourself to actually put in that 100% and not slack off from it?' let him name the gap. But past attempts were never actually asked for; the 30-30-30 protocol and the abandoned Ironman came out unprompted. The bigger issue is direction: the script's intent is 'the problem isn't effort, it's structure', and the rep landed the opposite — 'It's an internal switch above here... if you jump out of the boat, then there's nothing we can do' — putting the failure on the prospect's willpower rather than on the missing structure the programme sells.

P5.evidence: Ran near-verbatim. 'Where would you be in a year or two years from now, if you don't actually do it now?' → 'I'd just be in the same position, just like, meh.' Then 'would you be willing to settle for that version of yourself' and, when the answer wandered, a sharper re-ask: 'Are you willing to settle for you not putting in the effort, for you giving up, basically, and never achieving what you want to achieve?' → 'no, I'm not.' The line in the sand came via the devil-and-angel frame and landed: 'I would like a new identity. I want a new identity. I need a new identity.' Only 'why not?' was never asked.

P6.evidence: Belief question asked properly and tied to the support structure — 'do you believe that you can actually put yourself first this time and also stick with putting yourself first?... If we help you with all the other aspects of keeping you accountable, making sure you have the right program, focusing your nutrition.' He held the line until he had an unambiguous yes before presenting. The 'any reason you wouldn't go all in' variant only came after the pillars, and as a softer construction — 'do you feel like if you have that nutrition, the workouts, and also that lifelong success part with him in place, that you're also actually going to make that whole accountability aspect work'.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted — price given and 'Let's get started, or?' — so the phase applies. None of the four steps ran. No payment, and specifically the rep declined money the prospect offered ('maybe 500 bucks I could put down in the next week' / 'if you give me two weeks, I'd come up with a grand'), answering 'I don't think we should do it right now.' No Trevor onboarding call booked; the 21 August invite is a sales meeting with the rep. No agreement email, no signature, no welcome email, no Skool link, no onboarding questionnaire.

objection_plays.detail: Ran the permission line close to script — 'would you be willing to have like an open conversation, see if we can make something work?' — and got four of the six financial-picture items: cash on hand ('what would be available for you to just get started?'), savings ('do you have anything sort of stored away... any rainy day savings?'), credit score ('what's your credit score?' → mid 500s) and credit limits ('what would even be your credit limits?'). Never isolated first ('Finances aside — nothing else keeping you from 100%?'), never asked what is left each month after bills, never asked how many cards or used-versus-available, never asked about crypto, stocks or investments. Then abandoned the play mid-way and self-disqualified the prospect rather than building any structure — 'Okay, so I don't think we should do it right now.'

The August-commission deferral is a textbook 'not the right time'. The rep landed one scripted beat — 'you also just talked about not being able to push it forward one day... when you don't make a commitment for yourself, it's so, so, so easy to put it to the next day' — and then dropped it entirely. None of 'things never slow down', 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', 'what if all you had to do was show up', or 'the only thing you can control is right now'. He accepted a seven-week deferral from a prospect who had, ninety seconds earlier, said 'it can't be tomorrow, it has to be today'.

Script gap. The prospect objected to the accountability pillar on principle, not on price — 'I'm not so super jazzed with the whole sort of, yeah, I'll be part of the community... See, if I outsource my accountability, I've already lost.' There is no play for a prospect who rejects the delivery mechanism of a pillar while wanting the pillar itself, and the rep never resolved it; he agreed with the prospect's frame instead.

notes: Phases 3, 5 and 6 were genuinely excellent — the prospect thanked him twice for the mirror and gave an unforced identity-level yes before ever hearing a number. The call was then lost between the price and the hang-up: the open wallet stopped half-run, the rep refused two deposits the prospect volunteered, and a fully-committed buyer walked out with a date seven weeks away. Coach the back half, not the front. Secondary: baseline was skipped almost entirely, which is why the rep was improvising a nutrition and fasting protocol for a 49-year-old with an undiagnosed shoulder he had never asked a health-history question about.
